one_liner: Managed multi-cloud MongoDB database platform with programmatic administration API

evidence.claim: Atlas Administration API authenticates via OAuth 2.0 service accounts or API keys using HTTP Digest
evidence.quote: Learn how to authenticate Atlas Administration API requests using Service Accounts with OAuth 2.0 or API Keys with HTTP Digest Authentication to manage

evidence.claim: Service account client ID and secret are exchanged for an access token via OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow
evidence.quote: To authenticate with a Service Account, first exchange its client ID and secret for an access token using the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow.

evidence.claim: The Atlas Administration API is a REST API
evidence.quote: The Atlas Administration API follows the principles of the REST architectural style to expose a number of internal resources

evidence.claim: API covers many administrative object types (projects, users, clusters) with a full endpoint specification
evidence.quote: Atlas Administration API resources add, edit, or delete administrative objects within Atlas, including projects, users, and clusters.

evidence.claim: MongoDB ships an official MCP server for MongoDB and Atlas via its mongodb-js GitHub org and official docs
evidence.quote: A Model Context Protocol server to connect to MongoDB databases and MongoDB Atlas Clusters. Atlas API credentials are required to use the Atlas tools.

notes: Free Atlas signup ('Get started for free in minutes') allows creating service accounts/API keys, so credentials are self-serve. Gotchas: legacy API keys use HTTP Digest auth (unusual for HTTP clients; OAuth service accounts now preferred). Admin API does not read/write cluster data — data plane needs separate database user credentials. Atlas may enforce an API IP access list by default for new organizations. Official MCP server documented at mongodb.com/docs/mcp-server/get-started/.
